title: Mortgage Rates Post First Drop in Six Weeks to 6.67%; 15-Yr Falls to 5.96%
summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.67% the week of August 13, down from 6.69% - its first weekly decline in six weeks - while the 15-year fixed fell to 5.96% from 6.01%. A year ago the 30-year FRM averaged 6.58%, leaving financing only marginally above year-ago levels. Chief economist Sam Khater said the modest pullback, combined with for-sale inventory that keeps improving and listing prices running slightly below a year ago, is gradually shifting conditions toward buyers. Bankrate/Mortgage Research Center pegged the 30-year jumbo average near 6.84% as of mid-August.

title: Moishe Mana's Mana Common Buys Downtown Miami Former Post Office for $20.3M; Key Biscayne Home Sells for $14M
summary: Affiliates of Miami-based Stambul sold a five-story former post office at 100 Northeast First Avenue in downtown Miami, plus a neighboring 15,000 SF vacant lot at 54 Northeast 2nd Street, to Moishe Mana's Mana Common for $20.3 million - the week's priciest recorded South Florida commercial deal and another piece of Mana's long-running downtown Miami land assemblage (the office building spans about 35,600 SF). The week's top recorded home sale was in Key Biscayne, where an entity led by Concha Dominguez sold a 4,300 SF waterfront residence at 591 North Mashta Drive for $14 million - about $3,300 per square foot - to a company managed by Alvaro Castro Mendivil; the seller had paid just $3.2 million for the property in 2004.

title: Palm Beach's Seabreeze Estate Sells for $17.1M to Red Ventures CEO; Fort Lauderdale Home Fetches $16M
summary: Ric Elias, co-founder and CEO of Red Ventures, and his wife, Brenda, paid $17.1 million for a 4,900 SF home at 350 Seabreeze Avenue in Palm Beach - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. Seller Steven K. Hudson had bought the property for $15.8 million just three months earlier, in May (Christopher Leavitt held the listing and Jack Rooney brought the buyer, both of Douglas Elliman). In Fort Lauderdale, a 7,000 SF home at 1721 Southeast 11th Street - listed at $24.9 million a year ago - sold for $16 million, with an entity tied to Alon Steiger selling to Arlene G. Inch, chairwoman and owner of TransPak.

title: Aviation Exec Pays $19M for Surf Club Four Seasons Condo in Surfside
summary: Private-aviation executive William Papariella and accountant Michael Deo paid $19 million, through an LLC, for unit 307 in the south tower of the Four Seasons Residences at the Surf Club at 9001 Collins Avenue in Surfside - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. The 4,000 SF, four-bedroom, four-and-a-half-bath condo traded for about $4,800 per square foot. The seller, a trust tied to Richard Gold that had paid $10.4 million for the unit in 2021, realized an 83% gain in five years - a mark of how durable trophy oceanfront-condo pricing has been across Miami-Dade's barrier-island market.

title: MLG Sells Lake Worth's Savona Grand Apartments for $64.8M; Holman Sheds FTL Honda Dealership for $44.8M
summary: Affiliates of Wisconsin-based MLG Legacy Fund Investments sold Savona Grand, a garden-style apartment community at 7132 Colony Club Drive in Lake Worth, for $64.8 million - the week's top recorded South Florida commercial trade and a sign of continued institutional appetite for stabilized Palm Beach County rentals. Holman Automotive shed the Stoler Honda of Fort Lauderdale dealership at 12 East Sunrise Boulevard - about 96,000 SF of buildings - for $44.8 million, and the week's priciest recorded home sale was in Hillsboro Beach, where auto-industry executive Mike Manley sold a 9,000 SF oceanfront house at 955 Hillsboro Mile for $14.5 million.

title: Starwood Buys Two Miami-Dade Affordable Housing Communities for $63.8M
summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management paid a combined $63.8 million for two Miami-Dade affordable-housing rental communities, buying from the Gatehouse Group. Starwood paid $34 million for Magnolia Landing, a 150-unit, 20-building complex built in 2011 on 4.8 acres at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court in the Naranja area, and $29.75 million for Lafayette Square, a 160-unit, 19-story building on 1.2 acres at 150 Northeast 79th Street in Miami's Little River neighborhood. CBRE Capital Markets arranged a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan for the deal, which underscores growing institutional appetite for income-restricted rentals as market-rate multifamily activity moderates.
source: Commercial Observer / Commercial Real Estate Direct

title: Witkoff's $97M Shore Club, Related's Gallery at Lummus Top South Florida Permits
summary: South Florida's largest construction permits for the week ending August 5 were led by a $97 million phased new-construction permit for The Shore Club Private Collection at 1901 Collins Avenue in Miami Beach - Witkoff and Monroe Capital's roughly 481,200 SF luxury condo-and-hotel project (about 45 residences and 79 hotel rooms), which lined up $430 million in construction financing in 2023. The second-largest was a $74.5 million permit for the Related Group's Gallery at Lummus, a 415,500 SF apartment project at 395 Northwest First Street in Miami. The pipeline highlights how ultra-luxury coastal condos and large rental towers continue to drive the region's development activity.

title: Rivani Buys Miami Beach's 404 Washington Office-Retail Building for $31.5M
summary: Local developer Rivani paid $31.5 million - about $201 per square foot - for 404 Washington, a 156,752 SF office-and-retail building in Miami Beach, buying from Dominion Partners LP of Sunny Isles Beach. The purchase reflects continued investor interest in well-located South Beach commercial space even as broader South Florida office and retail sales volume cooled in the first half of 2026.
source: Commercial Real Estate Direct / South Florida Business Journal

title: Fisher Island Condo Sells for $15M; Margate Medical Complex Trades for $14.7M
summary: Software executive Mark Sutcliffe paid $15 million for a 3,600 SF condo at 7811 Fisher Island Drive in Miami - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (three bedrooms, three-and-a-half baths, plus about 2,100 SF of terraces), buying from a company led by Olga Postolnikov. Also trading was a Miami home at 7426 Southwest 49th Place, which a trust bought for $9.3 million from entrepreneur Juan Tavares and Naila Gonzalez. The region's priciest recorded commercial deal was a Margate medical-office complex at 3251 and 3271-3285 North State Road 7, which changed hands for $14.7 million.

title: Miami's Kiaora Street New-Build Sells for $22.5M; Harbor Group Pays $109M for a SoFla Property
summary: A trust paid $22.5 million for a newly built 8,500 SF home at 4040 Kiaora Street in Miami - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (six bedrooms, seven-and-a-half baths, with a guest house). Other notable trades included a $9.9 million Fort Lauderdale waterfront home at 4 Isla Bahia Drive, bought by Andrea Naticchione, and an $18 million vacant waterfront lot at 10312 West Broadview Drive in Bay Harbor Islands, which a family trust sold to an affiliate of David Burstyn's Winston Capital Management. In the week's top commercial deal, Norfolk, Virginia-based Harbor Group International paid $109 million for a South Florida commercial property.

title: Bal Harbour Oceanfront Condo Sells for $14.5M to Lead the Week's Deals
summary: A trust paid $14.5 million - about $3,600 per square foot - for a 4,000 SF oceanfront corner condo at 10201 Collins Avenue in Bal Harbour, the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (three bedrooms, four-and-a-half baths, with a terrace and ocean views), buying from a company led by Jason Claxton. The week's priciest commercial deal was in Lantana, where Miami-based Cherry Oak Management sold an assisted-living facility at 6026 Old Congress Road for $8.4 million. Also trading: a Lauderhill shopping center at 7100-7200 West Commercial Boulevard that sold for $6.8 million, from an entity tied to investor Allen Chelminsky.

title: Pinecrest Development Lot Sells for $14.5M; Doral Dealership Site Trades for $23M
summary: Financier Mauro Ivan Korlaet Araya and lifestyle-and-fashion influencer Daniela Fernandez Nazer paid $14.5 million for a vacant 1.1-acre lot at 9601 Southwest 67th Avenue in Pinecrest - the week's top recorded South Florida residential deal, a land price that underscores how scarce large buildable parcels have become in the affluent village. The week's most expensive commercial sale was a used-car dealership property at 8505 Northwest 12th Street in Doral, which changed hands for $23 million, reflecting continued investor demand for infill Miami-Dade commercial land.

title: Hallandale Beach's Millennium Plaza Mixed-Use Property Trades for $40M
summary: AS Hallandale Investment FL paid $40 million - about $209 per square foot - for Millennium Plaza, a 191,084 SF mixed-use retail-and-office property at 2500 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard in Hallandale Beach, roughly 14 miles south of Fort Lauderdale. The purchase adds to a wave of capital targeting Hallandale Beach, a dense, transit-adjacent submarket between Fort Lauderdale and Miami where developers have been assembling sites for mixed-use and residential redevelopment. Necessity-oriented, infill commercial assets in built-out coastal Broward continue to trade even as broader South Florida commercial volume cooled in the first half of 2026.

title: Boca Raton's Royal Palm Estate Sells for $21.5M; Willow Bridge Buys Fort Lauderdale Dev Site for $24.7M
summary: A trust paid $21.5 million for a newly built 9,400 SF home at 1642 Sabal Palm Drive in Boca Raton's Royal Palm Yacht and Country Club - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale (seven bedrooms, eight-and-a-half baths). Sellers John and Mary Hargrove had paid $6 million for it a year earlier, and it last asked just under $23 million (David Roberts of Royal Palm Properties held the listing; Douglas Elliman brought the buyer). The top commercial deal was a Fort Lauderdale development site at 1040 Bayview Drive, which an affiliate of Atlanta-based Willow Bridge Property Company bought for $24.7 million from a Procacci Development Corporation entity that had filed plans for a 259-unit mixed-use project. Also closing: a $9.3 million Miami two-home lot at 1650 Micanopy Avenue and an $8.2 million Opa-locka auto-services facility sold by a Longpoint Realty affiliate.

title: CIP Real Estate Pays $99M for Coconut Creek's Lyons Corporate Park
summary: CIP Real Estate paid $99 million - about $293 per square foot - for Lyons Corporate Park, a 337,392 SF multi-building industrial park at 6601 Lyons Road in Coconut Creek, roughly seven miles southwest of Boca Raton, buying from Industrial Development Co. and Lyons Corporate Park Co. LLLP. It was among South Florida's largest commercial trades of the week and reinforces how infill, shallow-bay industrial remains the region's most sought-after commercial asset class even as multifamily, office and retail sales volume cooled in the first half of 2026. Separately, the week's priciest recorded home sale was a newly built 6,900 SF house at 340 San Marco Drive in Fort Lauderdale that traded for $9.5 million (about $1,400 per square foot), sold by an entity tied to MDS Energy Development CEO Michael Snyder.
source: Commercial Real Estate Direct / The Real Deal

title: Kimco Realty Buys Two Broward Grocery-Anchored Centers for $109M
summary: Kimco Realty paid $109 million for two grocery-anchored Broward shopping centers, buying from KPR Centers. The larger deal was Sunshine Plaza, a 245,744 SF Publix- and Marshalls-anchored center on about 19 acres at 4017-4299 West Commercial Boulevard in Tamarac, for $56 million. Kimco paid $53 million for Pompano Marketplace, a 254,749 SF center at 1115-1117 South Federal Highway anchored by a Walmart Neighborhood Market. The purchases extend the REIT's push into necessity-based, grocery-anchored retail in dense South Florida submarkets - a segment that has held its value even as broader commercial volume cooled in the first half.
